children: , the artificial-intelligence chip and computing-platform powerhouse, won a major vote of confidence from Stifel after its fiscal second-quarter report. The firm lifted its price target to $315 from $282, pointing to approximately 42.9% upside from Friday's midday price of $220.41. Yet the stock fell about 3.3% after exploding 8.7% higher Thursday.

The business is still firing on every cylinder. Revenue more than doubled to $96.2 billion, with the data-center engine generating a staggering $89 billion. Management now sees third-quarter revenue near $108 billion, representing another 12.3% sequential increase, while Stifel expects Vera Rubin to deliver roughly 20% of next quarter's data-center sales. The pressure point is margin: guidance calls for 74%, down from 75%.

This pullback looks more like digestion than rejection. Thursday's rally created approximately $441.5 billion in market value, while Friday's decline erased roughly $180 billionnearly 41% of that one-session windfall. The GF Score of 90/100 keeps Nvidia firmly in elite territory, powered by exceptional profitability, growth and financial strength. But the weak GF Value reading sends an equally sharp message: the company is crushing expectations, and the stock is already charging investors heavily for that dominance.

title: Nvidia Drops 3.3% as $315 Target Meets a $108 Billion Test
